title: Animations and maps
text: Read layers want include map, e.g. raster file bathymetry use basemap polygons e.g. countries, national park boundaries points e.g. colony tagging location
code: # make colony dataframe, make it spatial and add CRS using sf package colony <- data.frame(colony = "Bird Island", lon = -38.03, lat = -54) %>%   st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat")) %>%   st_set_crs(4326)  # read countries from rnaturalearth at medium res library(rnaturalearth) land <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

title: Animations and maps
text: ’re going test maps animations first 30 days data.
code: # subset the tracking data to the first 30 days, to test our animation df_sub <- df %>%   dplyr::filter(date_time <= (min(df$date_time) + lubridate::days(30)))

title: Animations and maps
text: Next, assemble map using ggplot2. Add sf layers using geom_sf, terra layers using tidyterra’s functions geom_spatraster (rasters) geom_spatvector (vectors), add tidytracks layer using geom_event_path paths geom_event_point points.
code: # make the map map <- ggplot() +   geom_event_path(     data = df_sub, aes(col = bird_id), # tracks layer     size = 1.5, lineend = "round"   ) + # rounded line ends look smoother   geom_sf(data = land, fill = "grey50", col = NA) + # land polygons   geom_sf(data = colony, pch = 24, fill = "yellow") # add colony layer # print the map map

title: Animations and maps
text: Use ggplot2 functions coord_cartesian coord_sf change limits plot (alternatively, can crop layers required area making plot). coord_sf can also change projection.
code: # define south polar LAEA projection for plotting my_crs <- paste0(   "+proj=laea +lat_0=-90 +lon_0=0 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 ",   "+datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs" )  # you can use st_coordinates to get min/max coordinates of your tracking data range(st_coordinates(df)[, "X"]) ## [1] -179.8794  179.7600 range(st_coordinates(df)[, "Y"]) ## [1] -63.10255 -30.57208  # update extent of map using extent of tracking data map <- map +   coord_sf(     crs = my_crs, # change projection to LAEA South Polar     # NB. lims must be in the units of the target CRS, so we need to     # transform the data to that crs using st_transform     xlim = range(st_coordinates(st_transform(df_sub, my_crs))[, "X"]),     ylim = range(st_coordinates(st_transform(df_sub, my_crs))[, "Y"])   ) map

title: Animations and maps
text: Animate map using animate_map(). produces gganim object (ggplot2 object extra animation logic). use animate function gganimate package render animation object. gganim object attribute called n_timesteps. number unique timestamps tracking data used make plot. ensure smooth animation, need render least many frames time steps tracking data.
code: map_anim <- animate_map(   p = map, # our ggplot map   wake_length = 0.3, # proportion of total animation time   label_format = "%B %d" # month and date )  class(map_anim) # the gganim object ## [1] "gganim"          "ggplot2::ggplot" "ggplot"          "ggplot2::gg"     ## [5] "S7_object"       "gg" attr(map_anim, "n_timesteps") # number of time steps in animation ## [1] 60

title: Animations and maps
text: Now, render animation using gganimate::animate(). default, gganimate uses 100 frames. change using nframes parameter. can specify length animation using two three parameters: nframes: number frames render (default 100) fps: framerate frames/second (default 10) duration: duration animation seconds (default) use suggested number frames, duration 20 seconds. Depending number frames, rendering take minutes longer. See gganimate documentation information different renderer options making animation. can also save frame image file use software bind video. save animation file, use gganimate’s anim_save() function default saves recent animation, similarly ggsave().
code: gganimate::animate(   plot = map_anim, # our ggplot with added animation   # Number of frames equals time steps in the data.   nframes = attr(map_anim, "n_timesteps"),   duration = 5, # video duration in seconds   renderer = av_renderer(), # default is gifski_renderer()   # optionally, specify width and height of output animation   width = 540, height = 400,   units = "px", res = 96 # w/h in pixels, res in dpi ) anim_save("example_animation.webm") # add appropriate file extension

title: Animations and maps
text: animation included tracking data paths using geom_event_path(). Let’s illustrate difference paths points re-creating using geom_event_point().  Points animations work best resolution tracking data high, points closer together.
code: # first, make the map and print it to check map <- ggplot() +   geom_event_point(data = df_sub, aes(col = bird_id), size = 3) + # tracks layer   geom_sf(data = land, fill = "grey50", col = NA) + # land polygons   geom_sf(data = colony, pch = 24, fill = "yellow") + # add colony layer   coord_sf(     crs = my_crs, # change projection and define limits     xlim = range(st_coordinates(st_transform(df_sub, my_crs))[, "X"]),     ylim = range(st_coordinates(st_transform(df_sub, my_crs))[, "Y"])   ) # print to check map # add animation map_anim2 <- animate_map(   p = map,   wake_length = 0.3,   label_format = "%B %d" ) # render the animation gganimate::animate(   plot = map_anim2,   nframes = attr(map_anim2, "n_timesteps"),   duration = 5,   renderer = av_renderer(),   # optionally, specify width and height of output animation   width = 540, height = 400,   units = "px", res = 96 )

code: # load packages for acquiring, loading, and plotting rasters library(basemaps) library(terra) library(tidyterra)

title: Animations and maps
text: download using basemaps, need ask defined spatial extent (longitude/latitude) - usually want bounding box data can define extent programmatically, sometimes may want define manually, add buffer around data. Now extent rect, let’s download basemap.
code: # option 1: make a rectangle as the bounding box of all the data (in lon/lat) rect <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(df))  # option 2: specify the rectangle manually. I want the whole Southern Ocean # and up to the northern extent of my data (plus a 15 degree buffer) rect_coords <- c(   xmin = -180, # define the corners   xmax = 180,   ymin = -90,   ymax = max(st_coordinates(df)[, "Y"]) + 15 ) # add buffer # convert to an sfc object and set the CRS rect <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(rect_coords)) %>%   st_set_crs(4326) rect ## Geometry set for 1 feature  ## Geometry type: POLYGON ## Dimension:     XY ## Bounding box:  xmin: -180 ymin: -90 xmax: 180 ymax: -15.57208 ## Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84 ## POLYGON ((-180 -90, 180 -90, 180 -15.57208, -18... # download basemap as a terra spatRaster bmap <- basemap_terra(rect, map_service = "esri", map_type = "world_ocean_base") ## Loading basemap 'world_ocean_base' from map service 'esri'...

title: Animations and maps
text: Now assemble map. can add raster layer using tidyterra functions geom_spatraster (single layer e.g. bathymetry raster) geom_spatraster_rgb (RGB rasters layer red, green, blue).
code: # define new track colours to show up better on a blue background track_colours <- c(   "#FFD700", # Gold   "#FF6B35", # Orange   "#FF3399", # Hot pink   "#39FF14", # Neon green   "#FF4444", # Red   "#00FFCC", # Aqua   "#CC44FF", # Purple   "#FFFEE4", # White ish   "#FF7070", # Coral   "#CFFF04" # Neon yellow )  # assemble map map <- ggplot() +   geom_spatraster_rgb(data = bmap) + # basemap   geom_event_path(     data = df, aes(col = bird_id), size = 2, # tracks     lineend = "round"   ) +   scale_colour_manual(values = track_colours) + # track colours   geom_sf(data = colony, pch = 24, fill = "yellow") + # colony   coord_sf(crs = my_crs) # projection  # remove axes and gridlines so it looks neater map <- map +   theme_void() +   theme(     plot.background = element_rect(       fill = "white",       colour = "white"     )   ) map

code: # amt simulates movement from a redistribution kernel, which needs a map of # the landscape; this one is uniform, as the model below only depends on the # position of the animal landscape <- terra::rast(   xmin = -20000, xmax = 20000, ymin = -20000, ymax = 20000,   resolution = 100, crs = "EPSG:32630", vals = 0, names = "habitat" ) # an integrated step selection model: step lengths with a gamma distribution # (200 m per hour on average), turning angles with a von Mises distribution # (some directional persistence), and selection against locations far from # the centre of the home range, at (0, 0) movement_model <- amt::make_issf_model(   coefs = c("I(x2_^2 + y2_^2)" = -1e-6),   sl = amt::make_gamma_distr(shape = 2, scale = 100),   ta = amt::make_vonmises_distr(kappa = 1) )  # simulate a track with one location per hour simulate_track <- function(id, n_locations, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   start <- amt::make_start(     c(0, 0),     time = as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC"),     crs = 32630   )   kernel <- amt::redistribution_kernel(     movement_model,     start = start,     map = landscape,     # the model only uses the coordinates at the end of each step, so the     # landscape does not need to be queried     fun = function(xy, map) xy,     # the number of candidate steps drawn at each step (the default, 1e6, is     # much slower)     n.control = 1e3   )   path <- amt::simulate_path(kernel, n.steps = n_locations - 1)   data.frame(     id = id,     # moved to the centre of UTM zone 30N     x = path$x_ + 500000,     y = path$y_ + 4000000,     time = path$t_   ) } example_tracks <- lapply(1:3, function(i) {   simulate_track(     id = sprintf("medium_%03d", i),     n_locations = 500,     seed = 1000 + i   ) }) example_tracks <- do.call(rbind, example_tracks) ggplot(example_tracks, aes(x, y)) +   geom_path(colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +   facet_wrap(~id) +   coord_equal() +   labs(x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),     panel.grid.minor = element_blank()   )

code: # the input of each package, built from a data frame of locations make_inputs <- function(df) {   list(     tidytracks = mt_as_move2(       sf::st_as_sf(df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32630),       time_column = "time",       track_id_column = "id"     ),     # nolint next: object_usage_linter.     amt = amt::make_track(df, x, y, time, id = id, crs = 32630),     adehabitatHR = sp::SpatialPointsDataFrame(       df[, c("x", "y")],       data = data.frame(id = factor(df$id)),       proj4string = sp::CRS("EPSG:32630")     )   ) } # the grid on which the KDEs of all the tracks are estimated: the extent of # all the locations, extended on each side by half its longest side, with 200 # cells along its longest side. It is given to each package in its own way: # a bounding box and a resolution for tidytracks, a raster for amt, and the # centres of its cells for adehabitatHR. make_grid <- function(df) {   side <- max(diff(range(df$x)), diff(range(df$y)))   raster <- terra::rast(     xmin = min(df$x) - side / 2,     xmax = max(df$x) + side / 2,     ymin = min(df$y) - side / 2,     ymax = max(df$y) + side / 2,     resolution = side / 100,     crs = "EPSG:32630"   )   centres <- terra::xyFromCell(raster, seq_len(terra::ncell(raster)))   list(     bbox = c(       xmin = terra::xmin(raster),       ymin = terra::ymin(raster),       xmax = terra::xmax(raster),       ymax = terra::ymax(raster)     ),     res = terra::res(raster)[1],     raster = raster,     pixels = sp::SpatialPixels(       sp::SpatialPoints(centres, proj4string = sp::CRS("EPSG:32630"))     )   ) } iso_levels <- c(0.5, 0.95)  # The home range of each track, with each method and estimator, from the # input of its package (all the tracks) and the grid for the KDE. Each # estimator is named after its package (its first word), followed, for the # KDE of tidytracks, by its method. amt estimates the home range of a single # track, so it is applied to each track in turn. estimators <- list(   mcp = list(     tidytracks = function(input, grid) {       hr_tt_mcp(input, levels = iso_levels)     },     amt = function(input, grid) {       input |>         tidyr::nest(data = -id) |>         dplyr::mutate(hr = purrr::map(data, amt::hr_mcp, levels = iso_levels))     },     # adehabitatHR estimates a single level at a time     adehabitatHR = function(input, grid) {       lapply(iso_levels, function(level) {         adehabitatHR::mcp(input, percent = 100 * level, unout = "m2")       })     }   ),   # the UDs, with the reference bandwidth of each track, and tidytracks with   # both of its methods: binned (its default, which bins the locations onto   # the grid before smoothing them, as amt does) and exact (which evaluates   # the kernel of every location at every cell, as adehabitatHR does)   kde_ud = list(     "tidytracks (binned)" = function(input, grid) {       hr_tt_kde(         input,         h = "h_ref_indiv",         bbox = grid$bbox,         res = grid$res,         method = "binned"       )     },     "tidytracks (exact)" = function(input, grid) {       hr_tt_kde(         input,         h = "h_ref_indiv",         bbox = grid$bbox,         res = grid$res,         method = "exact"       )     },     amt = function(input, grid) {       input |>         tidyr::nest(data = -id) |>         dplyr::mutate(hr = purrr::map(data, amt::hr_kde, trast = grid$raster))     },     adehabitatHR = function(input, grid) {       adehabitatHR::kernelUD(input, h = "href", grid = grid$pixels)     }   ),   # the isopleths, starting from the locations (i.e. including the UDs)   kde_iso = list(     "tidytracks (binned)" = function(input, grid) {       hr_tt_kde(         input,         h = "h_ref_indiv",         bbox = grid$bbox,         res = grid$res,         levels = iso_levels,         method = "binned"       )     },     "tidytracks (exact)" = function(input, grid) {       hr_tt_kde(         input,         h = "h_ref_indiv",         bbox = grid$bbox,         res = grid$res,         levels = iso_levels,         method = "exact"       )     },     amt = function(input, grid) {       input |>         tidyr::nest(data = -id) |>         dplyr::mutate(hr = purrr::map(data, function(track) {           ud <- amt::hr_kde(track, trast = grid$raster, levels = iso_levels)           amt::hr_isopleths(ud)         }))     },     adehabitatHR = function(input, grid) {       ud <- adehabitatHR::kernelUD(input, h = "href", grid = grid$pixels)       lapply(iso_levels, function(level) {         adehabitatHR::getverticeshr(ud, percent = 100 * level, unout = "m2")       })     }   ),   # hulls of each location and its 10 nearest neighbours   locoh = list(     tidytracks = function(input, grid) {       hr_tt_locoh(input, n = 10, type = "k", levels = iso_levels)     },     amt = function(input, grid) {       input |>         tidyr::nest(data = -id) |>         dplyr::mutate(           hr = purrr::map(data, amt::hr_locoh, n = 10, levels = iso_levels)         )     },     # adehabitatHR counts the location itself in k, so k = 11 gives the     # same hulls; it returns the union of the hulls at every step, from which     # the isopleths are picked (see areas below)     adehabitatHR = function(input, grid) {       adehabitatHR::LoCoH.k(input, k = 11, unout = "m2")     }   ) ) # Time an estimator: a first run, which also gives its results, then, if it # took less than a minute, 5 more runs, whose median time is reported. time_estimator <- function(estimator, input, grid) {   start <- bench::hires_time()   result <- estimator(input, grid)   seconds <- as.numeric(bench::hires_time() - start)   runs <- 1   if (seconds < 60) {     timing <- bench::mark(       estimator(input, grid),       iterations = 5,       check = FALSE,       memory = FALSE,       filter_gc = FALSE     )     seconds <- as.numeric(timing$median)     runs <- 5   }   list(result = result, seconds = seconds, runs = runs) } timings <- list() area_results <- list() for (dataset in names(datasets)) {   df <- datasets[[dataset]]   inputs <- make_inputs(df)   grid <- make_grid(df)   n_tracks <- length(unique(df$id))   for (method in names(estimators)) {     for (estimator in names(estimators[[method]])) {       # the package of the estimator, i.e. the first word of its name (e.g.       # tidytracks for "tidytracks (exact)"), which gives its input and how       # to extract its areas       package <- sub(" .*", "", estimator)       # LoCoH in adehabitatHR would take hours on the long tracks (see the       # scaling below)       if (method == "locoh" && package == "adehabitatHR" && dataset == "long") {         next       }       message("Timing ", dataset, ", ", method, ", ", estimator)       timed <- time_estimator(         estimators[[method]][[estimator]],         inputs[[package]],         grid       )       timings[[length(timings) + 1]] <- data.frame(         dataset = dataset,         tracks = n_tracks,         locations = nrow(df) / n_tracks,         method = method,         package = package,         estimator = estimator,         seconds = timed$seconds,         runs = timed$runs       )       if (method %in% names(areas)) {         area_results[[length(area_results) + 1]] <- data.frame(           dataset = dataset,           method = method,           package = package,           estimator = estimator,           areas[[method]][[package]](timed$result)         )       }     }   } } timings <- do.call(rbind, timings) area_results <- do.call(rbind, area_results)
